clue.text: Smallwood, a joiner, takes carpenter for a meal

blocks.note: split as small (S, the clothing-label abbreviation) plus wood (teak, a hard tropical timber)
a conjunction is a word that joins clauses
Chips is the traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter

explanation.surface: A tradesman called Smallwood hires a carpenter to help with a job.
explanation.walkthrough: Smallwood looks like a surname but splits into small and wood; the 'joiner' is not a tradesman but the joining word AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak and chips is a classic British pub dish, a complete plate served at lunch or dinner.

clue.text: Nelson's point of departure?

blocks.note: surface reading: the harbour or place Admiral Nelson set sail from
setter's reading: departure as death, the place where Nelson departed this life

explanation.walkthrough: Admiral Nelson was killed in 1805 at the sea battle off this Spanish cape, so it was where he departed life rather than port.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson died aboard Victory during the famous naval battle off this Spanish cape, his final victory.

clue.text: Up above and outside look towards the stern

indicators.note: one word sits outside, wrapping around the other piece

blocks.note: aft is the nautical word for towards the back of a ship
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A sailor is told to glance upward and then toward the back of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft means high up overhead, especially in a ship's rigging, matching up above.

clue.text: Unsociably rings female when friend goes outside

indicators.note: the friend goes round the outside, so the other letters end up enclosed

blocks.note: an ally is a friend or supporter
two rings, each shaped like the letter O
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Someone phones a woman in a distant manner whenever her pal steps out.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting aloofly means keeping cool and distant from others, which is behaving unsociably.

clue.text: Leaves courses without one point!

indicators.note: without says one letter is taken away from the word

blocks.note: desserts are the sweet courses of a meal
S, south, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a series of classes, or meal courses, having earned no score.
explanation.walkthrough: DESSERTS has two S's; drop one and the courses become DESERTS. Leaves is a verb here, not foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon or walk out on, so deserts can stand for leaves as a verb.

clue.text: October 31, when Ella's worried about nothing

indicators.note: worried things are shaken about, so these letters are rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the remaining piece

blocks.note: taken as written
the name as written, the 's being 'is'
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A date on which a girl called Ella frets over nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowe'en, the eve of All Hallows, falls on the last day of October each year.

clue.text: Some chap I voted for - everything depends on him

indicators.note: some of the phrase means only a run of its letters is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of chap, the word I and the start of voted

explanation.surface: A voter backs a candidate on whom the whole outcome rests.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot person is the central figure on whom an operation turns and relies.

clue.text: It cleans wheels, cats and dogs! Very little gets through!

blocks.note: wheels is slang for a car
cats and dogs are household pets
wee is Scottish for very small
per means by way of or through

explanation.surface: A device that picks up wheel grit and pet hair, letting almost nothing slip past.
explanation.walkthrough: A carpet sweeper is a hand-pushed cleaner with rotating brushes; the clue's cats and dogs also suggest pet hair it collects.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet sweeper is a non-electric rolling brush device used to clear dirt from floors and rugs.

clue.text: TV programme covering unknown moneylender, about 50

indicators.note: about means around, so the lender's word surrounds the number

blocks.note: a blanket is a covering
y is an unknown in algebra
a bank lends money
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A television show reports on a shady moneylender of around fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: Blankety Blank was a long-running British TV game show hosted by Terry Wogan and later Les Dawson.
explanation.definitionFit: Blankety Blank is the name of a popular British television quiz show, so it is a TV programme.

clue.text: Similar articles must be on record - ring us

blocks.note: an and a are the two indefinite articles
a log is a written record, as on a ship
O is ring-shaped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor demands that comparable pieces be logged, then that someone phones.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous means comparable or corresponding in some respect, which is what similar means.

clue.text: Flush, like a girl in the '50s?

indicators.note: in places the girl inside the two numerals

blocks.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals, so two fifties are LL
Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone flushed red like a young woman of the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: The '50s looks like a decade but means two fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: Flush can mean exactly even with an adjoining surface, as level does.

clue.text: Design tin-opener factory

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a design or scheme
the opening letter of tin

explanation.surface: Somebody draws up a design for a can opener to be made in a works.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin-opener looks like a kitchen gadget but means the opening letter of tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an industrial works or manufacturing site, so it is a factory.

clue.text: Because obtained number is omitted?

blocks.note: for can mean because
got means obtained
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why a figure was left out after being received.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has been left out by oversight, so it is omitted.

clue.text: How a drunk holds on to things?

definitions.text: How a drunk holds on to things

blocks.clueFragment: How a drunk holds on to things
blocks.note: surface reading: the manner in which a drunk grips objects, clutching firmly for balance
setter's reading: tight is slang for drunk, so a drunk does everything in a tight manner

explanation.walkthrough: Tight is British slang for drunk, so the adverb doubles as 'in a drunk way' and 'with a firm grip'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means firmly or with a strong grip, and its root word is also slang for inebriated.

clue.text: Biting six-footer follows a sap!

blocks.note: a sap is a covered trench dug towards an enemy position
an ant is an insect, with six feet

explanation.surface: A tall man trails behind a fool, making a cutting remark.
explanation.walkthrough: Six-footer suggests a tall person and sap a fool, but they are an insect and a siege trench.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant remarks are sharp and incisive, cutting deep like a biting comment.

clue.text: Unproductive poster I left hidden

indicators.note: hidden says the letters lie concealed inside the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of poster through I into the start of left

explanation.surface: A billboard someone put up and abandoned out of sight achieved nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile means barren, incapable of producing offspring or results, so it is fruitless.

clue.text: Gin and tonic mixed with nothing is unrecognisable

indicators.note: mixed is used of a drink being stirred up, and here of letters jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A gin and tonic mixed with nothing else becomes a drink no one can identify.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incognito has a concealed identity, so they cannot be recognised by others.

clue.text: The most sunny point is outside an inlet

indicators.note: the point is outside, wrapped round the other word

blocks.note: west is a point of the compass
an arm of the sea is an inlet

explanation.surface: A weather report notes the sunniest spot is just beyond a coastal inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunny weather is warm, so the sunniest is also the hottest, the superlative form.

clue.text: Overlooking hospital blocks for cases of unconsciousness

indicators.note: overlooking something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
tranches are blocks, as of shares or money

explanation.surface: Building blocks with a view over a hospital house patients who are out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Overlooking looks like a view over the hospital but means ignoring its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a dazed half-conscious state, so trances are instances of unconsciousness.

clue.text: Steal someone's wages without getting worked up

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the wages wrap round the theft

blocks.note: pay is wages
nick is British slang for steal

explanation.surface: Someone pockets a worker's wage packet and stays perfectly calm about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Without reads as lacking, but here it means outside. Getting worked up is the definition, not the wordplay's end.
explanation.definitionFit: Panicky describes someone flustered and anxious, which is being agitated or worked up.

clue.text: By autumn mine is over; that's the snag

blocks.note: a pit is a coal mine
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A miner laments that the pit will be shut by autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' puts the mine above the autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or difficulty, the same as a snag or catch.

clue.text: Look forward to a selection of good books when pregnant

blocks.note: to expect is to anticipate
taken as written
NT, the New Testament, is a group of books from the Good Book, the Bible

explanation.surface: An expectant mother anticipates catching up on some fine reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectant woman is expecting a baby, an everyday euphemism for being with child.

clue.text: Order chief to be earlier

blocks.note: first meaning: the head of a religious order or house of monks
second meaning: coming before in time

explanation.surface: A boss commands a subordinate to arrive sooner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a monastic superior and also, as an adjective, means preceding in time.

clue.text: Land well in the middle and roll

indicators.note: in the middle keeps only the central letters of the word

blocks.note: to bag is to land or capture, as a catch
the two central letters of well

explanation.surface: A pilot touches down smoothly in the centre of the runway and taxis on.
explanation.walkthrough: Roll looks like a verb of motion but is a bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll, boiled before baking.

clue.text: Transport top brass round

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of brass
a ring is round, a circle

explanation.surface: Senior officers are ferried around in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Top brass suggests senior officers, but top only picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring is to carry or convey something to a place, which is to transport it.

clue.text: Girl I caught in time

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the period

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
taken as written
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A young woman says she was caught just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: It takes one against fuel to lead a political alliance

blocks.note: coal is a fuel
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
on can mean against, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: A party leader claims one opponent of fossil fuels can head a governing alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: To lead puts fuel at the front of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalition is a temporary union of parties formed to govern together.

clue.text: This biro Nigel designed for ex-soldiers

indicators.note: designed means made to a new pattern, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pen designer named Nigel made this ballpoint for veterans.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal British Legion is the UK charity for veterans of the armed forces; a biro is a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Legion is the main UK association of former servicemen and women, so it stands for ex-soldiers.
